description: Table 6, rendered as an image, is a four-column data table titled "Values of ε and ρ for austenite in 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels". Column headers are "Samples", "Aging states", "ε" (microstrain, unitless) and "ρ [m⁻²]" (dislocation density). The "Samples" column is merged into two blocks of four rows: "0.02Nb steels" and "0.04Nb steels". The "Aging states" column lists four conditions per steel, in identical order: "as-cast", "723 K/3 h", "773 K/3 h" and "823 K/3 h". For 0.02Nb steels the tabulated values are ε = 0.15, 0.09, 0.06, 0.02 with ρ = 1.11 × 10¹⁴, 6.66 × 10¹³, 4.44 × 10¹³ and 1.48 × 10¹³ m⁻² respectively. For 0.04Nb steels they are ε = 0.17, 0.10, 0.07, 0.06 with ρ = 2.51 × 10¹⁴, 1.48 × 10¹⁴, 1.03 × 10¹⁴ and 8.88 × 10¹³ m⁻². Both quantities decrease monotonically with increasing aging temperature in both steels, and at every aging state the 0.04Nb steel has the higher ε and higher ρ than the 0.02Nb steel. The table supplies the microstrain and dislocation-density inputs from which the citing text derives dislocation strengthening of austenite.

observations.observation: Table 6 has four columns: Samples, Aging states, ε, and ρ [m⁻²], with two sample blocks of four aging states each.
For as-cast 0.02Nb steel, ε = 0.15 and ρ = 1.11 × 10¹⁴ m⁻².
For 0.02Nb steel aged at 723 K/3 h, ε = 0.09 and ρ = 6.66 × 10¹³ m⁻²; at 773 K/3 h, ε = 0.06 and ρ = 4.44 × 10¹³ m⁻²; at 823 K/3 h, ε = 0.02 and ρ = 1.48 × 10¹³ m⁻².
For as-cast 0.04Nb steel, ε = 0.17 and ρ = 2.51 × 10¹⁴ m⁻².
For 0.04Nb steel aged at 723 K/3 h, ε = 0.10 and ρ = 1.48 × 10¹⁴ m⁻²; at 773 K/3 h, ε = 0.07 and ρ = 1.03 × 10¹⁴ m⁻²; at 823 K/3 h, ε = 0.06 and ρ = 8.88 × 10¹³ m⁻².
Both ε and ρ decrease monotonically as aging temperature rises from as-cast through 723, 773 and 823 K in both the 0.02Nb and the 0.04Nb steels.
At every corresponding aging state the 0.04Nb steel shows larger ε and larger ρ than the 0.02Nb steel.
The table is captioned as values of ε and ρ for austenite in 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels.
The citing text states that ε is calculated from the slope of the linear fitting graph of βcosθ–4sinθ, with the θ, β, βcosθ and 4sinθ values for austenite in 0.02Nb given in Table 5.
The citing text reports dislocation strengthening of austenite in as-cast 0.02Nb steel as 113.1 MPa, falling to 87.4, 70.8 and 40.2 MPa after aging at 723, 773 and 823 K respectively.
The citing text reports dislocation strengthening of austenite in 0.04Nb steel as 169.8 MPa in the as-cast state and 129.0, 106.1 and 98.9 MPa after aging at 723, 773 and 823 K respectively.
The calculated dislocation strengthening values track the tabulated ρ values, both decreasing with aging temperature and both being higher for 0.04Nb than 0.02Nb steel.
